messages:
Ben Carter: Dropping subject line variants for onboarding email v2 (Email #1, sent ~30 min after signup). Need a POV on value prop emphasis: latency vs cost vs reliability.

Ben Carter: Current draft options (rough):
A) “Your first LLM request in under 5 minutes”
B) “Ship faster with low-latency LLM inference”
C) “Lower your inference bill (without guesswork)”
D) “Production-grade LLM inference, minus the ops”
E) “Welcome to Redwood — your API key + quickstart”

Ben Carter: Goals: get them to create API key + first successful request. Also don’t want to overpromise.

Soojin Lee: +1 to not overpromising. “under 5 minutes” is attractive but risky. If we keep it, maybe soften: “in minutes” vs “under 5”.

Soojin Lee: Also “low-latency” is strong but can read like benchmark marketing. Reliability angle is safer/true, but may not feel urgent for day 0.

Tyler Benson: Deliverability lens: avoid “free credits” / “save $$” heavy spam vibes in subject line. Cost in the subject sometimes correlates with promotions tab. Not a hard rule but something to keep in mind.

Camila Reyes: For Email #1, I’d bias toward “do the thing now” (API key + hello world). Reliability can be body copy / second email.

Tessa Morgan: If we lead with “Production-grade…” it feels enterprise-y. These are mostly devs trying to see something work. I like E because it’s clear, but it’s not differentiated.

Ben Carter: Re: E, it’s straightforward but maybe too generic. We can A/B a generic utility vs a value prop.

Nikhil Sharma: For day-0 onboarding, latency matters only after they’ve shipped something. I’d position: “first request” + “streaming” as the wow. Reliability is a longer-term reason to stick.

Soojin Lee: Agree. If we want differentiation without hype: “Predictable performance” is better than “blazing fast”. Example: “Make your first request — predictable LLM inference” (still a little wordy).

Ben Carter: What about:
A2) “Make your first LLM request (quickstart inside)”
B2) “Make your first request — fast, reliable inference”

Tyler Benson: A2 is clean. Also helps match the CTA and landing. For B2, “fast, reliable” is fine but we should be consistent with messaging guidelines (we’ve been saying latency/cost/reliability in that order depending on context).

Soojin Lee: On “cost”: I’d avoid leading with it in subject line #1. We can test cost angle later for activated-but-stalled. For new signups, cost isn’t their pain yet.

Camila Reyes: +1. If we do a cost subject, make sure it’s concrete and not “save money now!!!”. But not for Email #1.

Tessa Morgan: Another angle: “Your API key is ready” feels transactional and gets opens. But we should only say that if the key is actually provisioned. (Is it?)

Ben Carter: Not auto-provisioned. They have to create it in Console.

Tessa Morgan: Then don’t say “ready”. Maybe: “Create your API key + run a hello world”.

Tyler Benson: Length check: keep it under ~55 chars for mobile. “Create your API key + run hello world” is borderline but ok.

Ben Carter: Proposed test:
Variant 1 (utility): “Create your API key + make your first request”
Variant 2 (value): “Make your first request with low-latency inference”

Soojin Lee: I’d tweak Variant 2: “Make your first request — low-latency inference” (less salesy).

Nikhil Sharma: Also “low-latency inference” might mean nothing to a new dev. Maybe “streaming responses” as a hook? “Make your first request — streaming on by default” (but is it by default?)

Ben Carter: Streaming is optional. So we can’t claim “by default”. But we can invite: “Try streaming in your first request”.

Camila Reyes: Keep Email #1 simple. Streaming could be Email #2 after first request, or a console nudge.

Tyler Benson: :thumbsup: for two-variant test. Make sure preview text reinforces the non-test subject line so we don’t confuse. Also avoid all-caps and exclamation.

Soojin Lee: Please include “Hosted API” somewhere in the body so they anchor what product this is. Also don’t say “guaranteed” or “SLA” in lifecycle onboarding copy.

Ben Carter: Cool. I’ll update copy doc + the experiment ticket.
Link to variants: https://drive.google.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-email-copy-variants-v2 (subject lines section)

Tessa Morgan: One more: can we add a “—” vs “+” test? Sometimes “+” reads spammy.

Tyler Benson: We can keep punctuation consistent across both variants to reduce confounds. Choose one.

Ben Carter: Good call. I’ll go with “—” (dash) in both.

Ben Carter: Final for this thread:
V1: “Create your API key — make your first request”
V2: “Make your first request — low-latency inference”

Soojin Lee: Works. V2 is ok as long as body copy clarifies “low-latency” = production tuning, not magic.

Camila Reyes: Ship it. Measure opens/clicks but call the winner based on activation lift, not vanity.

Tyler Benson: +1. I’ll add a note in the tracking sheet to watch promo tab placement + unsub/complaints by variant.

Ben Carter: Thanks all. I’ll post updated lines in #announcements once queued. :rocket: (reaction: :white_check_mark: from Camila Reyes)
